verdicts.title: Merge can allocate more TITN than it holds; no cap on total TGT merged, first-year snapshot then reverts

a.reden: Same missing cap on TGT amount leading to excess TITN claims and overflow in withdrawRemainingTitn

b.reden: Both describe the same issue: no cap on TGT merged causing claimable TITN to exceed contract balance and underflow in withdrawRemainingTitn.

verdicts.title: Owner can withdraw any token, including users' claimable TITN, at any time

a.reden: The candidate describes an owner withdrawal issue, which is a different root cause than the known finding about missing limits on TGT amount and overflow in withdrawRemainingTitn.

b.reden: The candidate describes unrestricted owner withdrawal of any token, while the known finding [H-01] is about exceeding the hardcoded TGT exchange limit leading to claim failures; these are different ro

verdicts.title: Leftover TITN after year one is paid only to unclaimed merge holders, so early claimers lose out

a.reden: The candidate describes unfair leftover distribution, while the known finding concerns missing handling of TGTTOEXCHANGE limit and overflow, which are different root causes.

b.reden: The candidate addresses unfair distribution of leftover TITN to early vs late claimers, while the known finding [H-01] is about an overflow when TGTTOEXCHANGE is exceeded, a different root cause and i

verdicts.title: Merge at exactly 360 days accepts TGT but credits zero TITN

a.reden: Different root cause and logic; candidate describes timestamp edge case, known finding concerns exceeding hardcoded exchange limits and overflow

b.reden: The candidate describes a timing edge case causing zero credit, while the known finding is about exceeding a hardcoded exchange limit leading to insolvency.

verdicts.title: Deployer-minted supply and Arbitrum lock can strand tokens unless deployer is owner

a.reden: The candidate describes a token lock issue in Titn.sol unrelated to the MergeTgt overflow/limit bug in H-01

b.reden: The candidate describes a deployer mint and Arbitrum lock issue, while the known finding H-01 is about MergeTgt deposit overflow and exchange period handling.

verdicts.title: TITN deposited after the first withdrawRemainingTitn() call is outside the snapshot and is not distributed

a.reden: The candidate describes a snapshot timing issue, while the known finding concerns exceeding a hardcoded exchange limit and overflow, which are different root causes.

b.reden: The candidate describes a timing issue with deposits after the snapshot not being distributed, while the known finding H-01 is about exceeding TGTTOEXCHANGE causing overflow and claiming issues.
